insights: The Cesàro average C_A(N) of the new-denominator density ρ_A has a universal Ω(1/N) lower bound: C_A(N) ≥ 1/N for every increasing sequence, because ρ_A(0)=1 always (the first fraction has no prior denominator to avoid) pins the running total at ≥1.
The Ω(1/N) floor needs NO arithmetic of the sequence — just one boundary term plus nonnegativity — which is why it is universal, including for Haight's vanishing-average constructions.
The genuine rate content is the frequency of large ratios: C_A(N) ≥ #{k<N : ρ_A(k)≥1/2}/(2N), so C_A→0 forces the large-ratio indices to have density 0.
Prime terms give an explicit large-ratio source (ρ_A(k)≥1/2 when n_k prime), so C_A(N) ≥ (prime-term density)/2, and a vanishing-average (Haight-type) sequence must be prime-sparse.
